claims.text: MongoDB documents index edits as rebuilds: queries can continue using the old index definition during rebuilding, and MongoDB replaces the old index when the rebuild finishes. Application query-vector changes must be coordinated with the new index becoming ready. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The October 2, 2026 MRVQ preprint describes a dimension- and rate-elastic resident vector artifact, while reporting quality tradeoffs. It scopes any claim that all vector systems necessarily rebuild for every dimension change; it supplies no evidence that Atlas supports this mechanism. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

A December 15, 2023 MongoDB forum participant reported re-embedding 700,000 documents after a vector-dimension limit problem. This is a historical user account of migration work, not a measured price, rebuild benchmark, or statement of the current dimension limit. (low confidence)

Atlas Automated Embedding billing is token-based and includes index creation, document inserts and updates, and query embedding. A dimension-change migration budget should therefore include the tokens reprocessed during re-embedding, rather than treating the smaller output width as evidence that this migration is free. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Larger embeddings generally require more compute, memory, and storage; reducing dimensions may lower ongoing vector-serving costs. Both OpenAI and Qdrant recommend considering the quality/resource tradeoff, so lower dimensions should be evaluated against retrieval quality and migration expense rather than assumed to produce proportional invoice savings. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

For Atlas Automated Embedding (autoEmbed), changing numDimensions, model, or quantization regenerates both the index and embeddings and incurs additional embedding costs. This is a corpus-processing event, not merely a metadata edit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For self-managed embeddings stored in vector fields, numDimensions must match actual embedding length at index and query time. Editing the index definition alone does not transform stored vectors; prepare compatible embeddings and coordinate the query path with the replacement index. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For a model migration, stage new embeddings in a separate field and build a matching index before switching queries. MongoDB documents this pattern; Qdrant independently describes parallel old/new retrieval with dual writes. Budget temporary overlap and migration writes as well as embedding generation. (medium confidence)

Automated Embedding billing is token-based and includes index creation, document inserts/updates, and queries. A planning estimate for regeneration is reprocessed corpus tokens multiplied by the applicable model token rate, plus concurrent query/update usage and any incremental infrastructure or transfer charges; this is an estimate, not a documented fixed reindex fee. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

OpenAI documents shortening text-embedding-3 embeddings after generation by truncating the vector and renormalizing it. Inference: if suitable full-length embeddings are already retained, this can avoid a new embedding API pass for dimensionality reduction. It does not eliminate rewriting stored vectors or building a matching Atlas index, and does not override Atlas autoEmbed regeneration behavior. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Larger vectors generally consume more memory, disk, and compute; both OpenAI and Qdrant advise evaluating these costs alongside retrieval quality. Smaller target dimensions can reduce ongoing resource demand, but these sources establish no universal dollar saving or rebuild duration for Atlas. (medium confidence)

For self-managed embeddings, MongoDB requires numDimensions to match the stored and query vector width. Its model-migration procedure re-embeds documents into a new field and builds a new index with the successor dimensions; changing an index definition alone does not regenerate application-managed vectors. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For ordinary embedding-model migrations, MongoDB and Qdrant both describe re-embedding the corpus and keeping query and document embeddings aligned with their model. Equal dimensions alone do not establish compatible embedding spaces; MongoDB separately notes compatibility within the Voyage-4 series. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A cost estimate can separate re-embedding token usage from index build resources, vector storage, and the overlap period. MongoDB recommends retaining old fields and indexes during self-managed migration; Qdrant likewise retains old vectors during backfill. These support budgeting temporary coexistence, but do not establish a fixed Atlas surcharge or a universal doubling of the entire bill. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Evaluate the successor setup on representative application queries before cutover. MongoDB recommends a sample-based quality evaluation and waiting for the new index to be READY; Qdrant recommends comparing labeled retrieval metrics and retaining the old setup until the new model clears the acceptance bar. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
